evidence.source: Shuowen.org, received 說文解字 entry for 兩
evidence.field: entry text and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry defines 兩 as 24 zhu, the weight unit, and analyzes it as 从一、㒳, glossing 㒳 as ‘divide evenly’ and saying it also supplies sound. Duan Yucai treats the analysis as associative. This is a traditional lexicographic account, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original pictorial basis.
evidence.title: 說文解字「兩」 — Shuowen.org

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, character entry 兩
evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze, seal, manuscript and usage sections
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze forms written 㒳, sometimes with a top stroke, and says a Warring States bronze form writes 羊 in the middle as a sound marker. It presents the chariot-front/yoke interpretation as a proposal attributed to 于省吾. It reports bronze uses for a quantity (‘two’) and a weight unit, including 小臣宅簋 and 平宫鼎, and records no oracle-bone form in the entry.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 兩

evidence.source: 李運富、何余華, “两”字职用演变研究（一）
evidence.field: sections on graphic history and early use, published 2017-05-09
evidence.text: The authors report initial 㒳 forms in early Western Zhou bronzes, including 盝驹尊 and 卫盉; a form with a top stroke appears by the Spring and Autumn period and gradually replaces 㒳, becoming dominant after the Han. They review the traditional distinction between 㒳 for ‘two’ and 兩 for the weight unit, but adopt the view that they are one graph. Their own proposal derives the shape by modifying part of 車 to mark a pair of horses as a dedicated measure; they explicitly describe this as a hypothesis after raising objections to a straightforward vehicle depiction. They cite Western Zhou uses: 《小臣宅簋》 ‘金車，馬兩’ and 《小臣守簋盖》 ‘宾马两’ (early Western Zhou); 《㒼簋》 and 《𤼈鼎》 (mid-Western Zhou). The date and examples establish early measure uses, not the proposed graphic motivation or a secure semantic chain to all later senses.
evidence.title: “两”字职用演变研究（一）

evidence.source: 李運富、何余華, “两”字职用演变研究（一）
evidence.field: discussion of disputed 車 and 丙 analyses
evidence.text: The authors recount analyses connecting 兩 and 丙 to parts of a chariot, then question whether the shapes fit the vehicle evidence and whether early uses show a noun meaning ‘vehicle’. They note that a supposed oracle-bone example for 丙 is uncertain and could instead show a measure word. Their alternative paired-horse measure account is explicitly conjectural. The source does not establish the original name or pronunciation of any depicted tool or vehicle part, so no borrowing based on such a name is supported here.
evidence.title: “两”字职用演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: entry 两 (兩), historical variant citations
evidence.text: The entry cites historical vulgar-form usage of 两 for 兩, including 《字學三正》 and 《干祿字書》 material. This shows 两 existed as a variant before modern simplified-character standardization; it does not by itself prove that the modern standard was directly derived from that specific older token.
evidence.title: [A00284-002] 两 (兩) — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: No glyph was visually inspected. The selected image is a modern digitally drawn bronze-script-style rendering; it is not evidence of an artifact’s exact shape or date.

The primary historical graphic account remains unsettled: Shuowen’s 一 + 㒳 analysis, the chariot-front hypothesis, and the dedicated paired-horse measure hypothesis are distinct accounts. The chariot and paired-horse proposals are not demonstrated original depictions.

The checked textual sources do not establish an absolute earliest attestation for every sense, a dated chain from paired-horse measure to numeral/both/pair, or the exact path by which weight and broader quantity uses developed.

The searched sources do not verify that two 丙 characters form the historical graph. No whole-graph borrowing from a tool or vehicle-part name is adopted; neither the name nor pronunciation of a proposed depicted object is independently established.

No verified paired Baxter–Sagart entries or full local Unihan reading rows were available in this invocation. Direct official Unihan character record pages were not inspected; modern readings and ancient sound relations are therefore omitted.

The Commons image page was not directly openable in the web tool. Search metadata identifies the direct file concept and rights, but did not verify an upload.wikimedia.org URL. The candidate is therefore recorded as a sourced lead rather than selected as a usable direct image.
The Sinica rights notice was inspected, but no character-specific Sinica page or exact glyph image was obtained; no Sinica candidate is proposed.

limitations.text: No image candidate met the requested directly verifiable image-URL and page-inspection standard in this run. Commons search surfaced a modern bronze-style redraw (ACC-b11980.svg) with a public-domain dedication, but the page failed to open and no direct upload URL could be verified. Sinica’s official CC0 query-image notice was verified, but the query did not yield a specific 兩 form image. No image is selected.
